                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# Passing Context for Dependency Injection - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2024-04-28, last updated: 2025-05-25, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1233990474986029156)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':wave: ---------------------- Yes, there is a standard pattern for passing the context object for database interaction to functions in Wasp.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'The context object is automatically passed to your operations (Queries and Actions) and APIs by Wasp.\n'[39m +

                    text: [32m'# Direct access to prisma - Wasp - Answer Overflow\n'[39m +

                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m'If you need to fetch your users directly in your server-side code, you can use the Prisma Client directly.\n'[39m +

                    type: [32m'text'[39m,
                    text: [32m'# How to properly type Prisma query results with included relations in Wasp? - Wasp\n'[39m +
                      [32m'created: 2025-02-28, last updated: 2025-08-27, [Read more](https://www.answeroverflow.com/m/1344854811715174400)\n'[39m +
                      [32m'\n'[39m +
                      [32m':wave: ---------------------- To properly type Prisma query results with included relations in Wasp, you need to adjust the type annotation for your query function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m"Here's how you can fix this:\n"[39m +
                      [32m'1. First, import the necessary types from Wasp:\n'[39m +
                      [32m"`import { GetProducts } from 'wasp/server/operations'`\n"[39m +
                      [32m"import { Product, File } from 'wasp/entities'\n"[39m +
                      [32m'2. Then, modify your query function type annotation to include the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'…\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +
                      [32m'Using the\n'[39m +
                      [32m'`satisfies` keyword is an excellent alternative approach to typing your query function in Wasp.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'This method allows TypeScript to infer the return type automatically based on the actual return value of your function.\n'[39m +
                      [32m'...\n'[39m +

This models the reply tree. - **Operations** (Wasp `query`/`action` declarations, callable on the client and auto-exposed on the server): implement exactly these four, with these exact names:   - `getPosts` (query): returns every post.   - `getCommentTree` (query): given a post, returns that post's comments as a nested tree (top-level comments, each with their replies nested recursively to any depth).   - `createComment` (action): creates a comment on a post, authored by a user (looked up by username), optionally as a reply to an existing comment.   - `deleteComment` (action): deletes a comment AND all of its descendant replies (cascade), so no orphaned replies remain. - **Seed**: define a Wasp seed function importable as `devSeed` (runnable via `wasp db seed devSeed`) that idempotently creates users with usernames `alice` and `bob`, and a post titled `Wasp Nested Comments`. Running it more than once must not create duplicates. - **Page**: a route `/post/:postId` whose page renders the nested comment thread for that post, showing every comment's text content.  ## Implementation Hints - Project path: `/home/user/nested-comments` - Start command: `wasp start` (this runs the client on port 3000 and the server on port 3001). Before starting, apply migrations with `wasp db migrate-dev` and run `wasp db seed devSeed`. - Wasp automatically exposes each operation on the server at `POST http://localhost:3001/operations/<kebab-cased-operation-name>` (e.g. `getCommentTree` -> `/operations/get-comment-tree`), so the operation names above must match exactly. - Model the reply tree with a Prisma self-relation on `Comment` (an optional `parentId` foreign key plus a `children` list). Build the nested tree in `getCommentTree` recursively. - Deleting a comment must remove the whole subtree beneath it; you can achieve this with a Prisma `onDelete: Cascade` referential action on the self-relation or by deleting descendants explicitly. - Operation argument and result shapes (these are checked exactly):   - `getPosts` takes no arguments and returns a JSON array; each element must include the keys `id` (number) and `title` (string).   - `createComment` takes `{ postId: number, authorUsername: string, content: string, parentId?: number | null }`. When `parentId` is omitted or null the comment is a top-level comment; otherwise it is a reply to that comment. It must return the created comment object, which must include its `id` (number).   - `getCommentTree` takes `{ postId: number }` and returns a JSON array of the post's top-level comment nodes (those with no parent). Every node in the tree (at every depth) must be an object with exactly these keys: `id` (number), `content` (string), `authorUsername` (string, the username of the comment's author), `parentId` (number or null), and `children` (an array of child comment nodes in the same shape). Sibling nodes must be ordered by ascending `id` at every level.   - `deleteComment` takes `{ commentId: number }`. - The `/post/:postId` page must display the `content` text of each comment in the post's thread.             [32m'  - Summarize the nature of the changes (eg. new feature, enhancement to an existing feature, bug fix, refactoring, test, docs, etc.). Ensure the message accurately reflects the changes and their purpose (i.e. "add" means a wholly new feature, "update" means an enhancement to an existing feature, "fix" means a bug fix, etc.).\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Do not commit files that likely contain secrets (.env, credentials.json, etc). Warn the user if they specifically request to commit those files\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Draft a concise (1-2 sentences) commit message that focuses on the "why" rather than the "what"\n'[39m +
            [32m'  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose\n'[39m +
            [32m'3. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following commands:\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Create the commit with a message ending with:\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Co-Authored-By: Pochi <noreply@getpochi.com>\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: Replace <Share URL> with the Share URL from system information if available. If not available, omit the " | [Task](...)" part.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.\n'[39m +
            [32m'   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.\n'[39m +
            [32m'4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook changes, retry the commit ONCE to include these automated changes. If it fails again, it usually means a pre-commit hook is preventing the commit. If the commit succeeds but you notice that files were modified by the pre-commit hook, you MUST amend your commit to include them.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Important notes:\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER update the git config\n'[39m +
            [32m'- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands\n'[39m +
            [32m'- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.\n'[39m +
            [32m'- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'# Creating pull requests\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use the gh command via the executeCommand tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.\n'[39m +

            [32m'1. You can call multiple tools in a single response. When multiple independent pieces of information are requested and all commands are likely to succeed, run multiple tool calls in parallel for optimal performance. run the following bash commands in parallel using the executeCommand tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:\n'[39m +

            [32m'When using the newTask tool, the agentType parameter is optional. Leave it empty (None) to launch a generic sub agent, or specify one of the available agent types below to select a specialized agent.\n'[39m +
            [32m'Available agent types and the tools they have access to:\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### browser\n'[39m +
            [32m'Web browser automation agent for navigating websites, interacting with pages, and extracting information. Uses agent-browser CLI for browser control, including headless sessions and optional local Chrome auto-connect.\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'### explore\n'[39m +
            [32m'Use this agent to explore the codebase when you need to: understand project structure, find where features are implemented, locate specific functions or classes, analyze code patterns, investigate how something works, search for examples or usage, or gather information before making changes.\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'- Configuration: "how do I configure Pochi?", "explain config options", "help me modify my config", "set up a new provider", "add an MCP server"\n'[39m +
            [32m'- Help & feedback: "join the discord", "report a bug", "where can I get help?"\n'[39m +
            [32m'\n'[39m +

            [32m'\n'[39m +
            [32m'Examples of user requests this agent shall trigger:\n'[39m +
